captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a circular pill cutter base designed to slice a pill into quarters. It features a flat, disc-shaped main body with a central concave recess shaped to cradle a convex pill. Two perpendicular thin slots cross through the center to guide cutting blades, while four small cylindrical alignment posts are distributed symmetrically near the outer edge.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric pill cutter base in OpenSCAD that can cut a pill into four equal pieces. The script must define a central concave pill holder matching a specified pill diameter and thickness, and feature thin guide slots for blades as well as four alignment posts around the perimeter.
captions.factory: The design uses a 'pill' module constructed by intersecting a cylinder with two spheres to model the convex shape of a pill. The 'base' module is built by unioning a large flat cylinder with four smaller cylindrical alignment posts defined in the 'post2' helper module. It then uses the difference operator to subtract the negative 'pill' shape from the center, cut two perpendicular thin rectangular channels using cubes, and add small beveled entries at the top of the slots using rotated cubes.
